Review Text:
The edges of these plates, regardless of gang, are consistently nicked and pitted. In most cases I was able to orient them in a way that the worst edges are the least visible, but I had two 2-Gang parts so awful that they had to be exchanged for the usual poor standard. I have access to three stores, so this is clearly a Leviton problem. I'd have substituted nylon over plastic, but as far as I can tell, only the medium size is available in that material, and they are shinier than the nominally matte-finished plastic plates.

To that end, the Decora line is supremely frustrating. The plastic plates and switches have more of a matte finish, but the outlets don't. Oh, and neither do the Decora dimmer switches, so you get gloss right next to matte. If I had it to do over again, I'd have gone with another brand entirely.

Product Name: SureSlide Ceiling Fan Control and Dimmer Switch for LED, Halogen and Incandescent Bulbs - White 66DF-W
Review Title: This switch has some issues and compatibility with an existing fan and its wiring may be low
Review Text:
The switch is problematic. I noticed on the back cover that the wire colors are not in agreement between English and Spanish. For example, the red wire is labeled in English that it goes to the fan but underneath in Spanish it says to the light.  The yellow wire is labeled in English that it goes to the light but underneath in Spanish it says it goes to the fan.  The instructions are not much help either. On the switch itself, the ground wire appears to be a more blue wire and is covered like the other three. I think someone could make a mistake in the connection.  The switch does not appear to use a neutral. Be aware the switch cannot be use as anything other than a single pole location control. The idea is you will be using the app to control the fan or the switch to manually change fan speed or light intensity. 

If you have two switches for you fan as in one by your bed for example and one by an entrance door to a bedroom, this may not work. Also be aware that while really any bulb type can be used with it, do not mix bulb types with your fan. The instructions tell you to keep all bulbs the same type. Obviously LED bulbs let you get to 300 watts; Other bulb types limit the switch's handling to 150 watts. 

This switch can only be used on ceiling paddle fans with split-capacitor or shaded pole motors. Thus its use is limited. The use of other fans outsides of these specs may cause overheating of the fan.  When I installed it, the lower end of the dimmed lights was really too bright and there was flickering. 

The biggest drawback is you have to have four wires (but one, the white neutral will not be used).  If you do not have a red wire or yellow wire to work with along with a black wire and ground then this switch is useless for you. You would have to run new wiring. So if anyone has an older fan in use for years and only a black, white, and ground wire...this is not going to work for you. There is just too much going on with this switch for it to be likely useful for anyone other than someone doing new work where sheetrock is not yet up and wiring can be done easily and correctly to match the wiring on this switch.  I have to think a new fan is needed to be able to work with the switch (split capacitor or shaded pole switch).  No it is not recommended to use the switch with any other motors or lights; that's in the instructions. Think about what you have and what you are doing and maybe this switch and the app will work well for you.

Review Title: Nice plug, tight holes for the wall plate attachment
Review Text: We have old wiring in our home and needed to remove a dimming switch. The problem is that the existing wall plate was cut to fit the space and a standard blank wall plate would not fit. So instead of leaving duck tape covering the opening on the existing wall plate, I bought this insert/blank to fill the void. It fits well and came with two screws to attach it to the junction box. The existing screws to re-attach the wall plate didn’t fit well into the insert when trying to do so through the wall plate (these screws DO NOT come with the insert). So I kind of did a “pilot” installation of the screws into the new insert without the wall plate in place which widened the screw holes enough to then attach the existing wall plate with the existing screws. The insert resembles a rocker switch (to a degree) but most importantly it blocks the interior wires (capped off but still live) from being touched/tampered with and has a nice aesthetic. Normally I would just purchase/install a blank wall plate, but that was not an option given the lack of space from the original installation necessitating use of the original (narrow) wall plate or using a hack saw to cut a standard sized wall plate (which, per the Home Depot employee) would not have ended up with a straight cut. Serves the purpose it was intended for, though re-attaching a wall plate is a little bit of a challenge.

     My next issue is the the lack of a 3/0 lug on the neutral terminal.  They do sell a lug you can buy separately, but if you read the instructions is specifically says to torque the lug before you install it on the neutral bar because the small fingers they put on the lug are so tiny that they will break if you tried to torque the lug after installing it on the neutral bar.

Product Name: 4 in. 2 Hour Fire Rated Round Baffle Slim Downlight, 1000 Lumens, 5 CCT Color Selectable 2700K-5000K, Dimmable
Review Title: A well-designed, reasonably priced, easy to install light
Review Text:
When I ordered this 4-1/4" 2 Hour Fire Rated Round Baffle Slim Downlight, 1000 Lumens, 5 CCT Color Selectable 2700K-5000K, Dimmable Recessed Light, I thought, what a novel idea: Cut a 4-1/4" hole in the ceiling sheetrock (or remove a standard ceiling fixture box), insert the hot, neutral and ground wires (no wirenuts required!) into the clever easy-peasy connections, squeeze the tensioners, insert the light and presto!  Well, after receipt of the fixture, reality intruded and my installation proved to be a bit of a challenge, mainly due to the construction of my 1976 walkout basement home.

Nearly every original light fixture in the house is of the canned recessed spotlight type.  The house has redundant heating systems, that is, forced air as well as electric radiant heating in the main level ceilings.  The latter means that cutting a new hole in the ceiling would sever the electric heating grid of that room, not an option.  That meant this new fixture would have to be downstairs and the best location site was in my music room over the desk.  The problem there is that it has a dropped-ceiling with plastic-covered insulated sections.  That would be a real problem because the tensioners would bite into the insulation and the plastic.  Hmmm.

What I thought might work out was having a piece of masonite with the circle cutout on top of the insulated panel to spread out the pressure of the tensioners.  Although it was some additional work, it turned out as hoped.

The fixture is wonderful addition to the room and illuminates the desk area very well.  I left the default setting on and see no reason to change it.  No need for a dimmer, I like it bright.  It only uses 12 watts.

Bottom line: it’s reasonably priced, easy to install in ordinary construction, is attractive, has a five year limited warranty and lights up the world, What more could you ask for?

Product Name: 4 in. 2 Hour Fire Rated Round Baffle Slim Downlight, 1000 Lumens, 5 CCT Color Selectable 2700K-5000K, Dimmable
Review Title: Great! 4-in LED recessed light with fire rating
Review Text:
This 4-in round LED light has a ton of output. That's really clean, nice and wide and color selectable. 
I don't have a way to test the fire rating, so I'm going to trust that the rating is good.   The red indication of the housing tells me it's fire rated which does not appear to have any effect on the light output. 
  The two clamps that hold this fixture inside the ceiling sheetrock are very strong.  I would imagine pulling them back out at a later time would be quite difficult, which keeps that gasket against the sheetrock to maintain that fire rating.  
  Install is very easy, and measurements are included in the instructions.  The instructions show a large wood cutting saw, don't use one of those.... The whole saw or she rock jab saw will do the job perfectly.  Not very much room for air with this 4-in round hole so be careful..
I would recommend this to anyone that needs a small light with large output, 12 LED Watts, and a fire rating.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 20 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-20R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5369E-BX
Review Title: Truly a major improvement in plug/connector safety and a major time saver.
Review Text:
•	This product design was new to me. I have installed many plugs and connectors on cords before, and if you have also, you know the challenges: twisting the stripped wire and forming a hook on the end, putting the hook under the terminal screw head and keeping it in place while you tighten the screw. 
•	Invariably, some of the wire strands come loose and the connection needs to be reworked.  I have even resorted to tinning the twisted wire strands to keep them together and prevent “wild hairs.”  The instructions for this device specifically say not to tin the ends.
•	Sliding the barrel over the plug/connector is also a challenge since the individual conductors need to make two 90-degree bends to get to the screw terminal.
•	Well…this device design eliminates all of these issues.  The twisted wire goes straight into a hole, you close three color-coded levers,  slide the barrel over the body, tighten three screws to hold the body in the barrel, and finally, tighten the strain relief clamp on the cable.  The last two steps are the same as the “old fashioned” type of plug/connector.
•	The barrel and body are keyed for easy assembly.  When the curved levers are closed to clamp the conductors, the curvature is the same as the inside of the barrel, so they cannot open or loosen. The body also has a stripping gauge on its side.
•	I estimate that it only takes 20% of the time to complete the total process and less than 5% of the time to secure the conductors themselves compared to the conventional style device.
•	I will search this device out when I need to make-up power cord or replace a plug or connector on an extension cord. The product is manufactured in Mexico and comes in a variety of NEMA configurations.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 20 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-20R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5369E-BX
Review Title: Leviton's Innovative Lever Lock Feature Is a Great Improvement
Review Text: The Leviton Lever Edge NEMA 5-20R (20A – 125V) Connector is almost everything I expect in a Leviton product: excellent design with quality manufacturing.  The connector didn’t disappoint me except for a couple of minor design aspects mentioned below.  Initially, I thought the Lever Edge series of products were a gimmick to differentiate Leviton products in the marketplace.  However, after my experience with this connector, I realize it’s a definite product improvement, especially in something like a cord end that experiences lots of movement.  I checked to see if a three-conductor #10 AWG STW cable (10-2 w/ground 600V rated service cable) would fit in the cable clamp (strain relief).  It did because there is a removable insert for larger sized cables (up to 0.72 inches).  The connector is rated for 10-14 AWG wires.  The levers snap into place firmly.  After clamping a #12 AWG wire into the connector, I gave it a good pull.  It remained tightly inserted.  The nylon body is robust, made of “impact modified nylon” according to the specification sheet available online.  The cable clamp and body retaining screws are compatible with square drive, Phillips, and straight slot screwdrivers.  The minor issues I noticed include: 1) the strip gauge in the instructions is not to scale, but an actual size one is printed on the side of the device, and 2) the long retaining screws are not captive.  If you drop one of those screws into an inaccessible location, you’re not likely to find a replacement.  Ultimately, I used connector to replace the receptacle end of a long #12 AWG extension cord.  I’m sure it will outlast the extension cord.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 20 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-20R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5369E-BX
Review Text: I have a drop cord that the end is coming off. I thought I would give this plug a try. It is easy to put an end on a cord. Make sure the cord is unplugged. Cut the cord so all the ends are fresh. Strip the insulation off the cord making sure not to nick the wires inside. Then strip the insulation off the individual wires. The plug comes with a strip guide and the instructions give dimensions. Disassemble the plug and put the black part over the cord. This plug is different because it has levers to lock the wires in place. This is why I gave it 4 stars. It’s hard to hold the plug, wire and lever at the same time. It does have a clear plastic plate so you can see the wire is in the correct position but I had a hard time holding everything. Usually the screws stay in the plug but they didn’t on this one. Reassemble the plug. There is a gauge on the bottom as to whether or not to use the block on the cord grip. This is the cord I use to start my snowblower and the plug is too big to fit in the housing for the electric start. A good thing is the cord is getting old and I should be able to move it to another drop cord in the future.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 20 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-20R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5369E-BX

Review Text: This is a sturdy plug connector for 3 wire electrical cord (10-14 gauge stranded wire only).  The connector has two parts that separate.  The wire connection is easy.  Pass through the strain relief part of the connector, strip the wires to the appropriate length, insert in the plug holes and swing the clamp lever shut.  Screw the two parts together, and tighten the strain relief clamp and you have a solid plug connector.  The wire lever clamps feel very secure.  I have no concerns about the wire connections in the plug.  While the clamps make it easy to connect the wires, you still need a screw driver to put the two parts together with the three screws provided, and you need it to tighten the two screws of the strain relief clamp.  I used this as a replacement end on a damaged heavy power cord, and am pleased with how it works.

Review Title: Poor quality: 4 out of 4 failed to hold torque.
Review Text: Bought one online and picked up in-store to install for home EV charging. The first receptacle stripped before reaching 75-inch pounds on all terminals but the ground (yes, i was using a torque wrench, and yes I'm 1000% sure it was set to in-lbs). I returned the first, and after reading the reviews here, bought three more hoping to hedge my bets and get at least one good one. No such luck! All three failed before reaching 75-inch pounds, most failed around 55-60 inch pounds  (I was stepping up torque slowly in 5-10 inch-lb increments). The last one of the batch held 75-inch pounds on three of the four terminals, but the last failed at just over 60 inch-lbs..... so close! Super disappointing, a family member installed one of these about 6 months ago with no issue, so not sure if there's a batch issue going on or what, but definitely a frustrating experience. Bought a Hubbell instead and had no issue holding torque the first time. Had no issues returning the first one, and don't expect any trouble with the rest, but save your time and buy something else.

Review Text: I bought this outlet, and a 50 amp GFCI breaker, a deep box and the two necessary wird clamps from HD.    I bought 7 feet of 6/3 Romex cable From a HD competitor that sells Romex by the foot, and also the necessary face plate. Ignore other posts saying that the $9 look alike outlet is OK for EV charging.  This outlet is a very different piece of equipment. Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 20 Amp 250 Volt Straight Blade Plug, NEMA 6-20P, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5466E-BX
Review Text:
This Leviton Lever Edge Easy Wiring Plug is just the thing to make adding a plug to an electrical cord, or replacing a damaged one.
It's always a meticulously hard problem to wire the cord wires into a new plug.  First you have to strip just the right amount of insulation off each wire.  You need to get just the right length, so you don’t have any excess, that might touch another stripped wire (causing a dead and dangerous short).  But, you don't want it too short so you can get it wrapped around the screw, so you can tighten it.  Always a fight to get the wire stuffed in the tight area inside the plug.  Don’t forget to rap the wire, so it goes clockwise around the screws, otherwise it will come off and fray.  Then you cram everything together and hope it stays put.
No more of all that.  With the Leviton Lever Edge it’s a snap.  You strip the wire to the exact length, using the gauge marked right on the plug.  Open the locking levers, stick in the wires. Close the locking levers. Put the plug together with the attached screws, and your done.  “Easy peasy”!
This is the best thing since sliced bread.  You’ll love it.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 15 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-15R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5269E-BX
Review Title: Easy Black and White Lever Edge Connector
Review Text:
Positive: This Black & White Lever Edge 15 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector makes it really easy to repair or create a new plug. The packaging is standard for a plug, everything came in tact and it comes with instructions. What made this product stand out is the lever edges or things that you move when you insert your stripped wire. Another thing I really liked is the color coding of black, white and green you know easily where to insert the line, neutral and earth wires. Normally with other plugs like this, I base it off the blade of the connector or have to see that the bolt is silver or lighter colored for the neutral. This product came in handy as I used it to make a short intermediate extension cord with wires brought out for my current meter to check the current a device uses.

Negative: The only thing downside I could find with this product is that I question the strength of the spring that holds the wire or the lever edge. It felt pretty snug and strong after I placed the wire in and closed the lever. It is hard to gauge how strong it is compared to the usual screw and clamp. Besides that, it should be fine if using the strain relief.

Overall: This Black and White Lever Edge 15 Amp, 125 Volt, NEMA 5-15R connector makes it even easier to replace a broken extension cord or create your own. The lever edge allows you to insert stripped wire without having to screw it into the connector however you will need a screwdriver to complete assembling the connector. I would recommend this product to friends and family.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 15 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-15R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5269E-BX
Review Title: A quick and easy connector for 15 Amp 125 Volt applications
Review Text: In my opinion Leviton is one of the highest quality electrical product manufacturers in the world. This connector could be wired properly by either experienced electricians or DIY'rs. The innovative design is patent pending at the moment. It is "Industrial Grade" reflecting that one might find it being used in a hospital or manufacturing facility. The most unique feature is the locking levers which are color coded for fail-proof installation. This connector is for stranded wire only and it locks each wire in when properly stripped using the strip guage right on the connector. For added convenience, the levers lock open for insertion, then produce a "click" sound when closing/locking in the wires. The harness has a greater range than any I have seen before.

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 15 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-15R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5269E-BX
Review Text: If you've ever replaced a plug or socket on an extension cord, you know how big of a pain it is to cut the wires to just the right length, then struggle to wrap the wires around the terminals, and tighten the screws without the wire popping out!  These lever action connectors are a game changer!  Easy to cut the wires to the right length, strip off a little insulation, insert them into the holes, and flip the levers for a quick secure connection.  Easily cuts the time in half if not more!  Well worth the small extra cost.  The housing is made with very good quality heavy duty plastic.  I am using this in a manufacturing environment, and have no doubt they will hold up under industrial conditions.  These are my new favorite replacement connectors.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

Product Name: Black & White Lever Edge 15 Amp 125 Volt Straight Blade Connector, NEMA 5-15R, 2P, 3W, Industrial Grade 5269E-BX
Review Title: A great innovation for connecting wire cords faster.
Review Text:
A faster way of connecting wires and just flipping the levers to lock them in on this female electrical plug. it will work on 15amp 125volt (inner leaflet instructions state 15amp and 20amp, but not sure if that is printed to encompass all the products or not). It does say that this device will accomodate cords from 14/3 type SJ to 10/3 type S (the thickness from 0.36 in. to 0.72" round cords).
The lever action is pretty fast a simple to use, instead of tightening screw terminals. You do have to use two different types of screw drivers to unscrew the front part and the back part. I wish that it was made so that only one screw can be used, to make it even faster.

Review Text:
OK, I have two degrees in Electrical Engineering (no joke) and refused to let this switch get the best of me. After many hours of struggling to reverse-engineer it, and figure out my insanely complicated landing junction box, I solved it.
The very poor documentation with this sensor-switch neglects to tell you two very important items.
1. The sensor-switch requires one input to be an always-on, live input from the "branch circuit" (fuse box).
2. The remote switch (the other end of the 3-way switch duo) can effectively be replaced by a 2-way standard switch. One traveler is no longer a traveler, it's tied to live.

With those pieces of info, I solved my problem. The branch circuit arrived in the junction box where this sensor-switch was located.  Also, the load came off this same junction box.  I replaced the remote 3-way switch with a 2-way switch (ONLY).  My circuit:

Live (from branch circuit) - to the sensor-switch black wire next to green Ground.  Also goes to remote switch.
Neutral (from branch circuit) - goes to the load (lamp) and also to the sensor-switch neutral input.
Traveler (from remote switch) goes to the yellow input on the sensor-switch
Load (i.e. the live, switched, power) - connects to the MIDDLE black wire of the sensor-switch.

NOW, it functions:   
1. motion turns it on (I put this lowest sensitivity, darkest room light)
2. turns off after 1 minute
3. can be switched on or off manually by pushing the button on the sensor-switch
4. can be switched on manually, by toggling the remote 3-way switch
5. can be switched OFF manually, by toggling the remote 3-way switch TWO TIMES (click-and-click).

That last part is the NON-INTUITIVE part, but because the remote switch is (or is effectively) a 2-way switch, to get two functions out of it you have to do two things. Toggle it once, or Toggle it twice.  That's why I say it "Works as a 3-way switch (kind-of)". It works, but it's not super intuitive.  It's good enough for me though!

Product Name: Decora Motion Sensor In-Wall Switch 5A Single Pole or 3-Way in White
Review Title: Works as 3-way (sort-of) when you figure it out
Review Text:
I have 2 degrees in electrical engineering (no joke) and it took me hours to work this out, due to crappy instructions. This sensor-switch ALWAYS needs live on it. So they tell you to bypass one traveler on the remote, standard 3-way switch.  That has 1 traveler pinned to live, and the other traveler switched. So to turn on "remotely" you throw the remote switch. To turn off, you throw the remote switch twice.

Once you work that out, it does what you want. You can turn ON the light at either end, turn OFF the light at either end, and the light automatically goes out after the timer expires.  If you want, it can also go on when it detects motion.  Bob's your uncle, but more of an uncle-in-law.

If you have live entering the sensor-switch box from the panel, you can have a simpler wiring.  Jumper one sensor-switch lead to live, and also send live to the remote switch. You then simply have a 2-way switch at the remote end (ignoring one of the travelers).  That could be a bit confusing though.
There is also an alternative wiring, where you jumper the "live" to the sensor-switch inside the sensor-switch box, if you have live entering that junction box.

Product Name: Decora Smart Switch Z-Wave 800 Series in White (Neutral Wire Required)
Review Title: New design is both a blessing and a curse
Review Text:
I have previously installed the earlier generation of this switch and this one. This one now doesn't  have any terminal screws or ports to direct connect to from your box. Instead, 4 x small-gauge stranded wires are protruding out of it for which you are expected to make wire splices for each of them. The good part is that you have a bit more flexibility for fitting the oversized switch unit into the box since the connected wires are more flexible and forgiving than the 14 ga wites in the wall.

The bad however: hope you folks don't mind using wire nuts over lever nuts (WAGOs) or push-in connectors. All the extra splice connections in combo with the size of this switch does not leave room to use WAGOs, and the stranded wire (if you are selling this in North America Leviton, please stick with solid wire and save us the headaches) won't go into a push-in connector.

The installation aside, the switch works well and does what it is meant to do. I am planning to hook it into my security alarm's home automation system right away.

Two last tips:

1) if this isn't a sqap for an existing switch and you have the luxury of installing a new box, pay extra for the 3"deep (15 cu in volume per device) box. You will appreciate the extra space with this guy.

2) I found out the hard way that if you hook the thing up and the light is always on no matter what you press on the switch, it means you likely lost your neutral splice and need to re-check that connection. Moreover, if splicing the switch white wire to a bundle of multiple neutral wires, I suggest you strip it back an extra 30-50% from what it already is in order to get a good twist and good connection.
